prompt: Give the BookRef record a natural ordering by implementing Comparable: year ascending, ties broken by title. Complete compareTo in BookRef; the tests sort a fixed shuffled list.
explanation: Implementing Comparable gives a type a natural order that Collections.sort and Arrays.sort use automatically. The standard multi-key pattern appears here: compare the primary key first (Integer.compare on years -- safer than subtraction, which can overflow), and only when that comparison returns 0 fall through to the secondary key (String's own compareTo). Records can implement interfaces just like classes; only their superclass is fixed.
hints: Integer.compare(year, other.year) already returns the negative/zero/positive value compareTo needs for the years.
Only when the year comparison is 0 should the titles matter -- store the first result and test it before falling back.
Strings are themselves Comparable: title.compareTo(other.title) supplies the alphabetical tie-break.
